On release [b9222](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b9222) with the same commands in llama-server, the pattern is different, with the results matching no-MTP up to width 2 and then diverging:

```console
no speculative decoding:       output A
draft-mtp width 1:             output A
draft-mtp width 2:             output A
draft-mtp width 3:             output B
draft-mtp width 4:             output B
```
Can you try the original model? i.e. in BF16 or at least Q8_0.
This is expected - we use different kernels for different batch sizes.

@am17an with a Q8_0 (`-hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF:Q8_0`), now I do *not* reproduce the same issue. So this looks specific to the Q4_K_M quantization / kernel paths. (And regardless, it sounds like my expectations about identical MTP/non-MTP behavior were wrong due to the point that Georgi raised.)

So with Q8_0 everything agrees:

```console
no speculative decoding:       output A
draft-mtp width 1:             output A
draft-mtp width 2:             output A
draft-mtp width 3:             output A
draft-mtp width 4:             output A
draft-mtp width 5:             output A
```

Yes if you keep everything in F32 for flash attention you *may* approximate batch-invariant behavior. i.e. batch (t1, t2, t3) vs 3 batches (t1), (t2), (t3) are numerically close, because we do most other things in F32 accumulation.

To chime in, I am experiencing the same issue. I do data extraction in strict JSON schema output (Temperature 0) and enabling MTP introduces drift, Qewn3.6-27B passes my 150 cases extraction reference benchmark at 100%, but turning MTP on drops that number to 97% - it consistently skips or misclassifies a small number of (same) cases. This is reproducible across runs.
I am using Q6_K_XL, so this does not only occur on Q4_K_M . I'm on a RTX5090 so Q8 is not an option for me

Question on MTP vs non-MTP divergence (follows #23302 / this thread), with SYCL data from a different backend.

Setup: Intel Arc Pro B70 (SYCL), ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:full-intel-b10853, Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M (arch qwen35, `nextn_predict_layers = 1`, MTP layer embedded), `-fa on`, q8_0 KV, `--parallel 1`, `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-p-min 0.75`.

Greedy (temperature 0) output compared by md5 against the same server without speculation:

| task | n-max 0 | n-max 2 | n-max 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 296-token Python function | A | A (identical) | A (identical) |
| 700-token prose essay | B | C (differs) | D (differs) |

Speed gain was real: 26.5 tok/s baseline to 35 (prose) / 46-52 (code) / 43-46 (thinking mode), acceptance 78-98%. The divergent text reads as coherent. Unlike the b9222 report above (identical up to width 2), here it already differs at width 2.

Questions for the maintainers:
1. Is divergence at n-max 2 on SYCL expected, for the reason given above (different kernels for different batch sizes)?
2. Is there a supported way to make draft verification batch-invariant, for example keeping flash attention in F32, and does the SYCL backend have an equivalent switch? What is its cost?
3. For quality, is there a recommended check beyond comparing outputs (for instance comparing logits or KL divergence of the verified path against the baseline), since one report in this thread saw a task-level drop (100% to 97%) on a strict-JSON extraction benchmark with MTP on?

We are running a task-level quality comparison (hard reasoning tasks, thinking on, MTP n-max 3 vs the same model without MTP) and will post the result here if useful.

Follow-up with the task-level quality result I mentioned (same setup as my comment above: Arc Pro B70, SYCL, b10853, Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_M, thinking on, effort medium, `--reasoning-budget 8192`, `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75`, temperature 1.0).

Seven hard reasoning/coding tasks (programmatically scored, 3 runs each), MTP run compared with an earlier no-MTP run of the same harness, tasks and scorer (a different session on the same machine, so not a same-hour A/B):

| | no MTP | MTP n-max 3 |
|---|---|---|
| mean of per-task medians | 0.988 | 0.957 |
| decode (median) | 25.2 tok/s | 47.0 tok/s (1.87x) |
| median seconds per task | 266 | 146 |

Per task the scores are equal or better on 6 of 7 (json_patch 0.92 to 1.00); the whole difference is one task, rle_bitset (1.00, 1.00, 1.00 without MTP versus 0.60, 1.00, 0.70 with it). With 3 runs per cell and temperature 1.0 that is inside what I would call noise, but it is also not proof of no effect, so I will re-run that task with more samples. No crashes or garbage output in any run.

Take-away so far: on this backend the speedup is large and the divergence from non-speculative output did not show up as a systematic quality loss in thinking mode, though one task may be sensitive. Happy to run a specific check if the maintainers have one in mind.

@agnaylor
